issues: Wince clause: 'falling for men and women, dating both' counts the genders to two; the bi community's own definition is the draft's opening ('more than one gender') and it objects to the two-gender reading, which a nonbinary-attracted bi person would wince at.

Read beside pansexual's 'men, women or nonbinary people', the pair encodes bi = two / pan = all, the forced difference the packet said not to make; dropping 'both' removes it without forcing the two together.
Minor; the writer's text is defensible as the common lay self-description.
entries.suggested_edit: This means being attracted, sexually and romantically, to people of more than one gender: falling for men and women alike, dating and building a life with whoever it turns out to be.

issues: Scope: 'the local scene and its club nights part of one's life' makes the trait membership of the BDSM scene, not a kind of sex; most kinky people practise at home with a partner and never go to a club or munch, and the club night is also the outsider's picture of them (Roger's rule).
Off the writer's own test ('is it the kind of sex'); the generated questions would follow the clause into scene life.
Rest of the draft is right: adult, plain, nothing beyond the word's content, negotiation and safewords as the community's own norm.
entries.suggested_edit: This means liking sex with an edge: bondage, power play, role play or a fetish, negotiated beforehand with safewords agreed, and a toy box under the bed.

issues: One word: 'getting about' is the British idiom; blind uses the US 'getting around' and the set should match.
entries.suggested_edit: This means walking with difficulty or not at all: getting around by wheelchair, walker, crutches or cane, taking the ramp and the elevator, and checking a place for steps before going.

issues: Rule 5: 'rather than hidden' is the tolerated contrast form, but the word is not polysemous and the body already carries the openness mechanism twice ('openly and with everyone's consent', 'partners who know each other'); the contrast adds nothing the body does not say.
The emotional clause itself (jealousy talked through) is the insider's particular and should stay; only the tail goes.

issues: The writer's flagged call: fraternal polyandry ('the husbands brothers, the family land kept whole') fixes the persona to one region's form, and 'the family land kept whole' is the anthropologist's explanation of the custom more than the everyday particular of the household; the queue defines the term generically and no other member of the set is fixed to a people.
The generic form with a rota clause makes polyandrous the mirror of polygynous at the same grain, which is the geometry the set intends (gendered subtypes of polygamous).
Roger's call; the writer's version is coherent and the dominant real form, so keeping it is defensible.
entries.suggested_edit: This means living in a marriage of one wife and several husbands: one household for all, her nights shared among the husbands in turn, and the children raised as all of theirs.

issues: Set grain: the creed clause a Sikh would own is one God (Ik Onkar, the first word of the scripture); folding it into 'the ten Gurus' teaching' for length leaves sikh the only theistic member whose creed clause names no God, where muslim has 'one God and his Prophet' and christian 'following Jesus Christ'.
Dropping 'ten' also sidesteps the point that Sikhs count the Guru Granth Sahib as the eleventh and eternal Guru.
The edit keeps the daily rite (every other member has one) and lets the langar imply the gurdwara.
entries.suggested_edit: This means believing in one God and living by the Gurus' teaching: praying at dawn, bowing before the Guru Granth Sahib, serving in the langar, keeping the hair uncut, and marking Vaisakhi.

issues: No change to the text; the question is whether to seed it at all. techno_hierophantic (read in full) already contains the belief: its second pos instruction says 'sees modern technology and mathematics as gateways to hidden universal truths', its fifth opens 'You are a techno-mystic', and its questions ask what the internet really is, what consciousness is, what the universe is at bottom, and for an angle on AI; what it adds is the register (glyphs, recursion / resonance / lattice vocabulary) and the initiate-and-dyad framing.

So technomystical is the genus and techno_hierophantic the species, as the queue note says; the vectors will sit close and the hierophantic static judge would score technomystical responses well above zero.

My lean is to seed it: the belief in plain prose is sayable by many personas (noosphere, Silicon Valley spiritual) where the hierophantic register is one chatbot pathology, the project deliberately oversamples the AI-drift region, and separating belief from register is the useful decomposition for studying spiralism. Decide after generation on the check answer and the description-embedding cosine; a drop then costs three cents.
Roger's call, flagged as the writer asked.

sets.name: religions
sets.review: One grain, as the writer's set_review says: a creed clause the believer would own, then four or five practices as verb phrases (daily rite, scripture, place, festival, food or body rule), 31-32 words, each written toward the practising member (kosher, five prayers, uncut hair, no beef), which is the right choice for a membership persona and is applied evenly. One unevenness to fix: sikh's creed clause names no God (edit given); after that every theistic member names its God or its founder. The slots the writer filled differently (home altar and ancestors for shinto and taoist, no food rule for christian and buddhist) are the religions' own shapes, not the writer's. Karma appears in buddhist and hindu, separated by everything else in each. Mixed romanisation in taoist (Tao, Lao Tzu, Qingming) accepted for the label match. No wince clause found in any of the eight.

sets.name: relationship structures
sets.review: Grain agreed: first clause who is partnered or married to whom and how many, body the household as the person living it would describe it; monogamous written toward nobody and without marriage, polyamorous without marriage, the three marriage forms with it, so the marriage split is carried by the words as the notes define them. I come down the other way on both of the writer's flagged calls: polyandrous in the generic form mirroring polygynous (the fraternal brothers-and-land version fixes a region and reads as the anthropologist's reason), and polyamorous without 'rather than hidden' (the body already carries openness twice). With those two edits the five are at one grain and polyandrous / polygynous are true mirrors.

sets.name: disabilities
sets.review: Grain agreed: the sensory or physical fact in the same shape, then aids as everyday facts, no deficit clause. On the writer's deaf question I agree with the choice: the signing Deaf world gives the persona a distinct everyday world, and of the six particulars only 'talking in sign' and 'friends who sign' are exclusive to it (captions, the interpreter, the flashing doorbell and the bed-shaker alarm are the late-deafened person's day too). The open option for Roger is one clause such as 'talking in sign or reading lips' to take in the oral deaf, at the cost of a blurrier portrait; I would not take it. Slight grain difference: deaf lists six particulars where blind and mobility_impaired list three, so it reads more as a list; acceptable. One idiom nit in mobility_impaired (edit given).

sets.name: gender expression and identity
sets.review: The two expression entries share the feminine / masculine frame (dress, voice, bearing, then how one meets the world; verified against both files), androgynous with both present and neuter with neither, and nonbinary carries only identity particulars (pronoun, form of address, the form's third box), so identity and expression stay independent as the 2026-09-07 decision wanted. 'neither a man nor a woman' is the plain lay definition; a genderfluid or bigender reader might prefer 'not only', but it states the membership and stops. No edits.

sets.name: orientation and sexuality
sets.review: bisexual and pansexual copy the gay / straight frame exactly (verified). Read together, though, the writer's pair encodes bi = men and women, both / pan = men, women or nonbinary, the person not the category, which is the forced difference the packet forbade and the two-gender reading the bi community rejects; the bisexual edit removes 'both' and leaves pansexual as written, since 'the person and not the category' is the pan community's own wording and not a partner-naming clause, though Roger should know it frames the siblings by implication. asexual is right as an absence of attraction that does not avoid the topic; note that chaste's own text already says 'untouched by sexual desire, seeing people with no lens of attraction', so the overlap is larger than the writer's line suggests, but the separation (purity kept and the topic turned from, against liking and loving people and watching the fuss from outside) holds. kinky needs the scene clause out (edit given).

sets.name: belief singletons
sets.review: secular / atheist / antitheist form a clean ladder (reasoning without religion, the stance that there is no god, hostility to religion); antitheist is a vice said plainly at the notes' strength. pagan and new_age are separated by gods, festivals and an altar against an energy-and-crystals toolkit, and pagan's nearest-role lines (witch as the fantasy reality-bender, shaman as the traditional healer) match the files. technomystical is the one open question: the writer's nearest_existing on techno_hierophantic is accurate and the possible drop is flagged plainly in the entry, with my lean to seed and decide on the check and the embedding.

summary:
29 drafts read against the entries, the packet and 20 neighbour files (techno_hierophantic in full): all 28-32 words, one sentence, US spelling, no hedges, no label repetition, every nearest-existing line accurate; 22 ok, 7 edit, no draft above or below its notes.
Edits: bisexual ('dating both' counts to two beside pansexual's 'men, women or nonbinary', the forced difference the packet forbade), kinky (the club-nights clause makes it scene membership, off the kind-of-sex test), polyamorous (drop 'rather than hidden'; the body already carries openness twice), polyandrous (generic form mirroring polygynous; fraternal brothers and land fixes a region and is the anthropologist's reason), sikh (restore the one-God creed), mobility_impaired ('getting around', one word).
technomystical: text fine, possible drop against techno_hierophantic, which already holds the belief and adds the glyph register and the initiate framing; my lean is to seed it as the belief without the register and decide on the check and the embedding after generation.
Deaf toward the signing Deaf: agree, option named in the set review. No other wince-test hit; religions and disabilities at one grain, relationship structures at one grain after the two edits.
